chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Informal sessions and the quartet format with the World's Greatest Jazz Band
summary: She likes the freer sessions; with the band she sings with a quartet that takes turns filling in like a jam session.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: So anyway, those first three recordings you made for the Monmouth-Evergreen Label kind of set you off again.
In a relatively structured kind of way. But since then you've become more free wheeling?

Right, which I like. Well, I did the arrangement - well, when I first went out with The World's Greatest Jazz Band, after I finished the engagement at the River Boat with Bobby, just he and Vic Dickerson and a rhythm section and myself, and following that engagement I went to the Down Beat with The World's Greatest Jazz Band. Well you know the World's Greatest Jazz Band started out with about nine or ten pieces. But after we went to Europe the first time we went with the full band. You know it costs allot of money to take all these musicians over there all the time, so the Band sort of dwindled down to seven pieces. And we made some - they made some records over there. I think there are two

albums that the World's Greatest Jazz Band made over there and I've got two selections on each one.
Yeah, one was made in Sweden. And then when I was in . . .
I also notice that on everything you do with the World's Greatest Jazz Band you're only, in fact, accompanied by a quartet.

That's right. Well, one of the things that happened, you know, when the band was say like nine pieces they were playing arrangements and they were reading them and they had band stands in front of them. And not only that, when they would get up to play an arrangement, well they like to stand up, but they were sitting down and reading; number two they'd have to put on their glasses and I don't think these guys wanted to put on these glasses. So what they did was they memorized the arrangements and then they did away with the band- stand. And of course that was good for me because I didn't have to have any music except piano parts. And basically I like to work with a trio. If there's a horn, one horn, fine. If there is more than one horn they each
